meta.ai_assistance: The preprocessing script that produced this file was written with the help of Claude (Anthropic), an AI assistant. The values themselves come from the NASA and USGS sources listed in DATA_SOURCES.md; no values were generated by the AI.
meta.description: Habitat and science stops chosen by the team from data/candidate_sites.json. Names, briefings and facts are NASA text; 'task' is left empty for the science team.
meta.source: NASA Mars Trek points of interest and Perseverance traverse (see DATA_SOURCES.md)

habitat.name: Habitat (Perseverance landing site)
habitat.note: Start of Perseverance's earliest drive (sol 14) in NASA's traverse data. NASA calls the landing site 'Octavia E. Butler'.

stops.name: Séítah
stops.briefing: The first close-up look at the oldest rocks in Jezero crater visited by Perseverance happened in this spot. Dubbed the Séítah formation, these rocks revealed a geologic story that no one had anticipated.

stops.name: Delta front
stops.briefing: After years of anticipation starting with compelling views from orbit, Perseverance arrived at the front of the ancient delta deposit that motivated the selection of Jezero crater for the Mars 2020 mission. Mastcam-Z responded with the biggest panorama yet taken.

stops.name: Belva crater
stops.briefing: After traversing much of the Jezero delta fan deposit, Perseverance stopped to peer into its largest crater, called Belva, to get a look into the third dimension of the deposit, revealing details of its stratigraphy.
